Álvaro Obregón.analysis: Álvaro Obregón has a mixed labor profile with roughly 42% professionals, 39% in trade and services, and 17% in industry, mirroring a balanced, urban economy with minimal agriculture. Its education supply is large (1,931 basic and 411 higher-education schools; ~17.5% higher level), backed by 29 public health centers (~5.8% of the city’s total). It concentrates about 7.7% of sports facilities, 4.4% of cultural venues, and 6.1% of recreational venues citywide, and hosts around 9.9% of the city’s restaurants. Mobility is solid but not central: 3 metro lines, 1 Metrobús line, 28 RTP routes, and a modest 2.5% of Ecobici stations. Green space averages 6.6 m² per resident, near the city middle, while housing quality is very high (near-universal basic services; ~3.45 persons per household). Safety indicators are mixed (general security near the lower-middle of the pack; women’s security around mid-range). Demographically it is large (~759k residents) with a moderate older share (~16%). Budget intensity is above average on both revenue indicators, suggesting strong commercial and rental markets.

description.es: Se ubica en la zona poniente y es una de las alcaldías más diversas en cuanto a paisaje y estilos de vida. Por un lado, tiene barrios populares y comunidades tradicionales; por otro, colonias residenciales de alto nivel y grandes corporativos. San Ángel es uno de sus tesoros: calles empedradas, casonas coloniales, museos y el famoso Bazar del Sábado que atrae a artistas y visitantes. También destacan sus barrancas, miradores naturales y zonas como Santa Fe (que se extiende en parte aquí), donde conviven universidades, corporativos y centros comerciales modernos.
description.en: Located in the western area, it is one of the most diverse boroughs in landscapes and lifestyles. On one hand, it has working-class neighborhoods and traditional communities; on the other, upscale residential areas and major corporate hubs. San Ángel is one of its treasures: cobblestone streets, colonial mansions, museums, and the famous Saturday Bazaar that draws artists and visitors. It also stands out for its ravines, scenic viewpoints, and areas like Santa Fe (partly within the borough), where universities, corporate offices, and modern shopping centers coexist.

Azcapotzalco.analysis: Azcapotzalco shows an urban professional tilt (about 48% professionals) with substantial services and moderate industry; agriculture is almost nil. It has 1,155 basic and 116 higher-education schools (low higher-education share), 27 public health centers, and accounts for ~3.7% of sports, ~2.3% of cultural, and ~3.4% of recreational venues. Green space is relatively favorable (9.9 m² per resident). Transit access is diversified though not central (2 metro lines, 2 Metrobús lines, 9 RTP routes, and ~4.1% of Ecobici stations). Restaurants are ~3.1% of the city’s stock. Safety indicators trend below the city median (both general and women’s security on the lower side). Households are slightly smaller than average (~3.21 persons), housing quality is near-universal, and the population is moderately older. Commercial revenue intensity is modest on sales but moderate on rentals.

description.es: En el norte poniente, esta alcaldía tiene un fuerte legado industrial, pero también un gran sentido histórico y cultural. Sus barrios antiguos conservan iglesias coloniales, y su identidad se refleja en el orgullo “chintololo”. El Parque Bicentenario es uno de sus mayores atractivos: un espacio verde recuperado de terrenos industriales que hoy es pulmón de la ciudad. También ofrece espacios culturales como la Casa de Cultura Azcapotzalco y múltiples festividades tradicionales.
description.en: In the northwestern area, this borough has a strong industrial legacy as well as deep historical and cultural roots. Its old neighborhoods preserve colonial churches, and its identity is reflected in the local “chintololo” pride. Parque Bicentenario is one of its highlights: a green space reclaimed from industrial land that now serves as a city lung. It also offers cultural spaces like the Azcapotzalco House of Culture and many traditional festivities.

Benito Juárez.analysis: Benito Juárez has the city’s most professionalized workforce (~70% professionals), very low industry, and a strong services base. Education is robust (1,346 basic, 379 higher; ~22% higher-level), complemented by 25 health centers. It concentrates ~5.8% of sports, ~8.1% of cultural, and ~5.7% of recreational venues, and a high 13.7% share of restaurants. Mobility is excellent (4 metro and 3 Metrobús lines, 18 RTP routes, and ~31.5% of Ecobici stations). Green space per capita is scarce (2.2 m²), reflecting high density, but housing quality is among the city’s best and households are small (~2.46 persons). Safety is the city’s strongest both overall and for women. Demographically it skews older. Rental market intensity is among the highest; sales activity is also strong.

description.es: Conocida como una de las alcaldías con mayor calidad de vida, es una zona residencial de clase media y media alta, bien comunicada y con gran infraestructura urbana. Colonias como Del Valle, Narvarte, Portales y Nápoles destacan por sus parques, cafés, restaurantes y vida familiar. Aquí también se encuentran recintos culturales como el Polyforum Siqueiros y una importante cantidad de teatros. Es un espacio muy atractivo para quienes buscan una vida tranquila en el corazón de la ciudad.
description.en: Known as one of the boroughs with the highest quality of life, it is a middle and upper-middle-class residential area, well-connected and with strong urban infrastructure. Neighborhoods such as Del Valle, Narvarte, Portales, and Nápoles stand out for their parks, cafés, restaurants, and family-friendly life. It is also home to cultural venues like the Polyforum Siqueiros and a significant number of theaters. It’s highly attractive for those seeking a calm lifestyle in the heart of the city.

Coyoacán.analysis: Coyoacán’s workforce is highly professional (~55%) with low industry and strong services. It offers 1,679 basic and 458 higher-education schools (~21% higher-level), 27 health centers, and an important cultural footprint (~8.3% of city cultural venues), plus ~6.0% of sports and ~5.9% of recreational facilities. It holds ~8.2% of restaurants. Transit is good (2 metro, 2 Metrobús, 31 RTP routes, a modest number of Ecobici stations). Green space per resident is ample at ~15 m². Safety is mid-range (general and women’s), housing quality is excellent, and households average ~3.2 persons. The population is sizeable (~614k) and comparatively older. Budget indicators show strong commercial activity in both sales and rentals.

description.es: Un símbolo cultural de la ciudad. Su centro histórico conserva la esencia de un pueblo mágico con calles empedradas, plazas arboladas y casonas virreinales. Es famoso por el Museo Frida Kahlo (Casa Azul), el Museo León Trotsky y el Centro de Coyoacán, lleno de cafés, artesanías y librerías. Además, alberga a la UNAM, Patrimonio Cultural de la Humanidad, que concentra vida estudiantil y académica. Es un punto de encuentro para quienes buscan arte, tradición y un ambiente bohemio.
description.en: A cultural symbol of the city. Its historic center preserves the essence of a magical town with cobblestone streets, tree-lined squares, and viceregal mansions. It’s famous for the Frida Kahlo Museum (Casa Azul), the León Trotsky Museum, and the Coyoacán center, full of cafés, crafts, and bookstores. It also hosts UNAM, a UNESCO World Heritage site, concentrating student and academic life. It’s a meeting point for those seeking art, tradition, and a bohemian atmosphere.

Cuajimalpa de Morelos.analysis: Cuajimalpa blends services (~40%) and industry (~17%) with a smaller but notable agricultural presence by city standards. Education is compact (857 basic, 63 higher; low higher-education share), and it has 14 health centers. It hosts ~2.7% of sports, ~0.9% of cultural, and ~2.9% of recreational venues, and ~3.1% of restaurants. Transit lacks rail-based coverage (no metro or Metrobús) but has 13 RTP routes. Green space is decent (10.3 m² per resident). Safety stands above average (both general and women’s), families are larger (~3.6 persons), and housing quality is high. The population is relatively young. Commercial revenue intensity is very strong, particularly on sales and rentals.

description.es: Situada en las montañas del poniente, combina naturaleza y modernidad. El Desierto de los Leones, con su convento y bosque protegido, es uno de los principales pulmones de la ciudad. Al mismo tiempo, en esta alcaldía se encuentra parte del distrito financiero de Santa Fe, con rascacielos, universidades, corporativos y uno de los centros comerciales más grandes de Latinoamérica. Esta dualidad entre lo rural y lo ultramoderno hace de Cuajimalpa un lugar muy particular.
description.en: Located in the western mountains, it combines nature and modernity. Desierto de los Leones, with its convent and protected forest, is one of the city’s major green lungs. At the same time, part of the Santa Fe financial district lies here, with skyscrapers, universities, corporate offices, and one of the largest shopping centers in Latin America. This duality between rural and ultramodern makes Cuajimalpa a very unique place.

Cuauhtémoc.analysis: Cuauhtémoc is a metropolitan core: a highly professional workforce (~51%), heavy in services, and minimal industry. It has a very large higher-education footprint (1,737 basic, 754 higher; ~30% higher-level) and the city’s largest cluster of health centers (70). It dominates cultural and recreational supply (~28.2% and ~16.5% of city totals, respectively), sports (~7.2%), and restaurants (~27.6%). Mobility is the strongest in the city (7 metro lines, 5 Metrobús lines, ~36% of Ecobici stations, 13 RTP routes). Green space per capita is limited (~3.6 m²) due to central density, but housing quality is excellent with small households (~2.75 persons). Safety is above average (general and for women), and the budget rental index is the city’s highest; sales are also strong.

description.es: El verdadero corazón de la Ciudad de México. Aquí se concentran los principales edificios históricos, políticos y culturales: el Zócalo, la Catedral Metropolitana, Bellas Artes, el Monumento a la Revolución y Paseo de la Reforma. Además, es sede de barrios emblemáticos como la Roma, Condesa y Juárez, conocidos por su vida cultural, gastronómica y nocturna. Es la alcaldía más visitada por turistas nacionales y extranjeros, y un centro donde la historia convive con la modernidad.
description.en: The true heart of Mexico City. It concentrates the main historical, political, and cultural buildings: the Zócalo, the Metropolitan Cathedral, Bellas Artes, the Monument to the Revolution, and Paseo de la Reforma. It is also home to emblematic neighborhoods like Roma, Condesa, and Juárez, known for their cultural, gastronomic, and nightlife scenes. It is the most visited borough by domestic and foreign tourists, where history coexists with modernity.

Gustavo A. Madero.analysis: Gustavo A. Madero’s economy mixes services (~41%) and industry (~17%) with a moderate share of professionals (~41%). It has extensive basic education (3,651 basic, 428 higher; low university share) and 58 health centers. It concentrates sizable shares of sports (~13.2%), recreational (~11.3%), and cultural (~6.8%) venues, and ~4.7% of restaurants. Mobility is strong on bus and rail (5 metro and 5 Metrobús lines, 18 RTP routes), though no Ecobici. Green space is moderate (6.7 m² per resident). Safety indicators rank on the lower side (both general and for women). Housing conditions are broadly good (~3.42 persons per household). Population is very large (~1.17M) with a mid-to-older profile, and budget intensity is moderate.

description.es: En el norte, es famosa a nivel mundial por albergar la Basílica de Guadalupe, uno de los recintos religiosos más visitados del planeta, que recibe millones de peregrinos cada diciembre. Además, tiene una importante zona natural en el Cerro del Chiquihuite y barrios con fuerte identidad cultural. Es una alcaldía de contrastes: tradición religiosa, zonas residenciales, mercados populares y espacios deportivos.
description.en: In the north, it is world-famous for the Basilica of Guadalupe, one of the most visited religious sites on the planet, which receives millions of pilgrims each December. It also has an important natural area on the Cerro del Chiquihuite and neighborhoods with a strong cultural identity. It is a borough of contrasts: religious tradition, residential areas, popular markets, and sports spaces.

Iztacalco.analysis: Iztacalco has a balanced urban economy (about 46% professionals, ~38% services, ~14% industry) and the smallest land area. It provides 1,149 basic and 82 higher-education schools (very low higher-education share) and 11 health centers (one of the lowest). It hosts ~4.1% of sports, ~2.7% of cultural, and ~2.9% of recreational venues, and a very small restaurant share. Mobility is quite good in rail and bus terms (5 metro, 3 Metrobús, 9 RTP routes) but lacks Ecobici coverage. Green space per resident is low (~5 m²). Safety indicators rank below average for both general and women’s security. Housing conditions are excellent, with ~3.43 persons per household. Budget intensity is relatively low.

description.es: La más pequeña en extensión, pero de gran relevancia histórica y cultural. Sus barrios como Santa Anita y la Asunción conservan tradiciones de pueblo originario. También es una alcaldía de grandes eventos: aquí se encuentra el Palacio de los Deportes y el Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez, sede del Gran Premio de México de Fórmula 1 y de conciertos internacionales. Iztacalco representa una mezcla entre tradición barrial y espacios modernos para espectáculos.
description.en: The smallest in area, yet of great historical and cultural relevance. Neighborhoods like Santa Anita and La Asunción preserve traditions of original towns. It is also a borough of major events: it is home to the Palacio de los Deportes and the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez, host of the Mexican Formula 1 Grand Prix and international concerts. Iztacalco represents a blend of neighborhood traditions and modern event venues.

Iztapalapa.analysis: Iztapalapa is the city’s most populous borough (~1.84M) with a working profile tilted toward services (~45%) and industry (~18%), and a lower professional share (~35%). It has the largest basic education network (4,241 basic) but few higher-education schools (212; ~4.8% share), and 65 health centers. It leads in sports (~18.1%) and recreational (~16.9%) venues and has a strong cultural share (~8.2%). Mobility is broad on buses and metro (3 metro, 2 Metrobús, 22 RTP routes), though no Ecobici. Green space per resident is limited (~5.4 m²) but total green area is large. Safety indicators are among the lowest in the city (general and women’s). Housing conditions are good with larger households (~3.61 persons). Budget intensity is mid-range, and restaurants account for ~3.6% of the city.

description.es: Es la alcaldía más poblada de la Ciudad de México y una de las más emblemáticas por su vida cultural y tradiciones. El Cerro de la Estrella, además de ser un importante sitio natural con vistas panorámicas de la ciudad, fue escenario de ceremonias prehispánicas como el Fuego Nuevo, lo que lo convierte en un lugar de gran valor histórico y espiritual.Además, sus barrios tradicionales conservan mercados muy vivos, templos antiguos y una vida comunitaria llena de costumbres que la hacen única. Es una alcaldía vibrante, llena de movimiento, con una identidad cultural que se refleja en sus fiestas, su gastronomía y sus espacios públicos renovados.
description.en: It is the most populated borough in Mexico City and one of the most emblematic for its cultural life and traditions. Cerro de la Estrella, beyond being an important natural site with panoramic city views, was the setting for pre-Hispanic ceremonies like the New Fire, making it a place of great historical and spiritual value. In addition, its traditional neighborhoods preserve lively markets, old temples, and a community life full of customs that make it unique. It is a vibrant borough, full of movement, with a cultural identity reflected in its festivals, gastronomy, and revitalized public spaces.

La Magdalena Contreras.analysis: La Magdalena Contreras has a services-driven workforce (~43%) with notable industry (~18%) and a modest professional share (~36%). Education infrastructure is compact (575 basic, 37 higher; very low higher-education share) and it has 14 health centers. It contributes ~3.1% of sports, ~1.2% of cultural, and ~1.6% of recreational venues citywide, and a small restaurant share. Transit is limited (no metro/Metrobús/Ecobici; 5 RTP routes). Green space per capita is modest (~5.5 m²). Safety is around mid-range (general slightly above average; women’s mid-range). Households are relatively large (~3.62 persons), and housing quality—while high—ranks slightly below other boroughs. Budget sales intensity is very strong; rentals are moderate.

description.es: Un oasis natural en la ciudad. Conserva ríos, cascadas y áreas boscosas, siendo el Parque Nacional Los Dinamos su principal atractivo para el ecoturismo. Sus pueblos originarios mantienen tradiciones y fiestas patronales que ofrecen un ambiente rural dentro de la urbe. Es la opción ideal para quienes buscan naturaleza, tranquilidad y aire fresco sin salir de la Ciudad de México.
description.en: A natural oasis in the city. It preserves rivers, waterfalls, and forested areas, with Los Dinamos National Park as its main ecotourism attraction. Its original towns maintain traditions and patron saint festivities that offer a rural atmosphere within the metropolis. It is ideal for those seeking nature, tranquility, and fresh air without leaving Mexico City.

Miguel Hidalgo.analysis: Miguel Hidalgo is highly professional (~59%) with strong services and low industry, and it stands out in culture (~13.1% of city cultural venues) and restaurants (~16.6%). It has 1,273 basic and 325 higher-education schools (~20% higher-level), 27 health centers, and excellent mobility (4 metro, 2 Metrobús, 23 RTP, ~20.5% of Ecobici stations). Green space per resident is among the city’s best (~15.4 m²). Safety is strong (general and women’s above average). Housing quality is excellent with smaller households (~2.81 persons). Budget indicators are the city’s highest for sales and near-top for rentals, underscoring an intense commercial-real estate market.

description.es: Mezcla lujo, cultura y naturaleza. Alberga colonias de alto nivel como Polanco y Lomas de Chapultepec, llenas de embajadas, restaurantes de alta gama y centros comerciales. También está el Bosque de Chapultepec, el parque urbano más grande de América Latina, con museos, zoológico y el Castillo de Chapultepec. Es centro empresarial, turístico y residencial, reflejando la modernidad y sofisticación de la ciudad.
description.en: It blends luxury, culture, and nature. It includes upscale neighborhoods like Polanco and Lomas de Chapultepec, full of embassies, high-end restaurants, and shopping centers. It also contains Chapultepec Park, the largest urban park in Latin America, with museums, a zoo, and Chapultepec Castle. It is a business, tourism, and residential center, reflecting the city’s modernity and sophistication.

Milpa Alta.analysis: Milpa Alta is the most rural and least urbanized borough: a services-and-industry mix with the city’s highest agricultural share (~7%) and the lowest professionalization (~23%). Education infrastructure is small (391 basic, 19 higher; very low higher-education share) and it has 16 health centers. It holds ~1.8% of sports and ~2.3% of cultural venues, and a minimal restaurant presence. Mobility is limited (no metro/Metrobús/Ecobici; 6 RTP routes). Green space per resident is very low (~2.2 m²), but the setting is semi-rural. Safety is mixed (general mid-range; women’s above average). Housing quality is lower than elsewhere but still broadly adequate, with larger households (~3.9 persons). Marriage rates are the highest citywide. Budget intensity is modest for sales and high for rentals.

description.es: La alcaldía más rural y menos urbanizada. Sus montañas, campos de cultivo y comunidades indígenas conservan un estilo de vida ligado a la tierra. Es famosa por la producción de nopal y por sus fiestas patronales llenas de tradición. Milpa Alta representa las raíces más profundas de la ciudad, con paisajes naturales y un ambiente distinto al ritmo urbano del resto de la capital.
description.en: The most rural and least urbanized borough. Its mountains, farmlands, and indigenous communities maintain a way of life tied to the land. It is famous for nopal production and traditional patron saint festivities. Milpa Alta represents the city’s deepest roots, with natural landscapes and a pace of life distinct from the urban rhythm of the rest of the capital.

Tláhuac.analysis: Tláhuac combines services (~45%) and industry (~20%) with a small agricultural base; professionalization is modest (~33%). It has 873 basic and 30 higher-education schools (the lowest higher-education share) and 21 health centers. It contributes ~4.7% of sports, ~3.7% of cultural, and ~3.4% of recreational venues, and a very small restaurant share. Mobility includes 1 metro line and 9 RTP routes (no Metrobús/Ecobici). Green space per resident is relatively good (~8.4 m²). Safety indicators are among the lowest (general at the bottom; women’s very low). Housing quality is good but somewhat below top boroughs, households are larger (~3.67 persons), and marriages are relatively common. Budget intensity is low for sales but high for rentals.

description.es: Ubicada al sureste de la Ciudad de México, Tláhuac es una de las alcaldías que mejor conserva la esencia del antiguo Valle de México. Su paisaje combina zonas urbanas en crecimiento con pueblos originarios, chinampas y áreas semirurales que ofrecen un ambiente distinto al de otras partes de la capital. Aún se puede apreciar un ritmo de vida más tranquilo, con tradiciones profundamente arraigadas en sus comunidades.
description.en: Located in the southeast of Mexico City, Tláhuac is one of the boroughs that best preserves the essence of the old Valley of Mexico. Its landscape combines growing urban areas with original towns, chinampas, and semi-rural zones that offer a different atmosphere from other parts of the capital. A calmer pace of life can still be felt, with deeply rooted traditions in its communities.

Tlalpan.analysis: Tlalpan is diverse, with ~44% professionals and a balanced services/industry mix. It offers 1,838 basic and 329 higher-education schools (~15% higher-level) and 40 health centers. It accounts for ~7.4% of sports, ~4.0% of cultural, and ~6.6% of recreational venues, and ~4.2% of restaurants. Green space is ample (~9.6 m² per resident), reflecting extensive natural areas. Mobility lacks metro but includes 2 Metrobús lines and 24 RTP routes. Safety sits around the middle (general and women’s). Housing quality is high but among the lower tier relative to other boroughs, with ~3.44 persons per household. Budget intensity is mid for sales and high for rentals.

description.es: La más grande en extensión territorial. Abarca desde áreas urbanas con hospitales y universidades, hasta zonas boscosas y montañosas como el Ajusco, muy visitado para senderismo y deportes de montaña. Su centro histórico conserva el ambiente de un pueblo con casonas coloniales, plazas y templos. Es una alcaldía diversa: científica, natural y cultural al mismo tiempo.
description.en: The largest in territorial extension. It spans from urban areas with hospitals and universities to forested and mountainous zones like Ajusco, popular for hiking and mountain sports. Its historic center preserves a small-town feel with colonial houses, squares, and temples. It is a diverse borough: scientific, natural, and cultural at the same time.

Venustiano Carranza.analysis: Venustiano Carranza has a services-oriented economy (~44%) with moderate professionals (~42%) and industry (~12.5%). It has 1,228 basic but just 23 higher-education schools (the lowest higher-education share), and 30 health centers. It contributes ~4.3% of sports, ~2.7% of cultural, and ~6.8% of recreational venues, and ~2.4% of restaurants. Mobility is strong in rail (6 metro, 2 Metrobús) with 9 RTP routes; it also hosts the city’s airport. Green space per resident is high (~13.6 m²). Safety is mixed (general around the middle; women’s slightly below average). Housing quality is excellent (~3.26 persons per household). Budget intensity is mid-range for both sales and rentals.

description.es: Parte de su importancia radica en que aquí se encuentra el Aeropuerto Internacional de la Ciudad de México (AICM), la principal puerta de entrada y salida del país. Además, Venustiano Carranza cuenta con colonias de gran tradición como la Moctezuma, Jamaica, con su famoso mercado de flores, y zonas residenciales. La alcaldía es, en pocas palabras, un lugar de paso y de encuentro, donde el comercio, la movilidad y la cultura popular se entrelazan de manera constante, haciéndola vital para el funcionamiento de la ciudad.
description.en: Part of its importance lies in hosting the Mexico City International Airport (AICM), the main gateway in and out of the country. In addition, Venustiano Carranza has traditional neighborhoods like Moctezuma, Jamaica with its famous flower market, and residential areas. In short, it is a place of passage and meeting, where commerce, mobility, and popular culture are constantly intertwined, making it vital for the city’s functioning.

Xochimilco.analysis: Xochimilco combines services (~42%) with notable industry (~17%) and one of the city’s higher agricultural shares (~2.7%). It provides 1,051 basic and 26 higher-education schools (very low higher-education share) and 23 health centers. It hosts ~5.4% of sports, ~3.1% of cultural, and ~2.9% of recreational venues, and a small restaurant footprint. Mobility is limited (no metro; 1 Metrobús line; 15 RTP routes; no Ecobici). Green space per resident is low (~5 m²). Safety indicators are among the lowest (general and the lowest for women’s security). Housing services are widely available, though good-condition rates are lower than city leaders; households are larger (~3.74 persons). Budget intensity is low for sales and relatively high for rentals.

description.es: Reconocida mundialmente y declarada Patrimonio Cultural de la Humanidad por la UNESCO, Xochimilco es una de las alcaldías más pintorescas y representativas de la Ciudad de México. Su mayor atractivo son las chinampas y canales. Xochimilco es un lugar donde tradición, cultura y naturaleza conviven de manera única. Representa el alma festiva y comunitaria de la Ciudad de México, siendo al mismo tiempo un símbolo nacional que conserva vivas costumbres que se remontan a la época prehispánica.
description.en: Recognized worldwide and declared a UNESCO World Heritage Cultural Site, Xochimilco is one of Mexico City’s most picturesque and representative boroughs. Its greatest attraction is the chinampas and canals. Xochimilco is a place where tradition, culture, and nature coexist in a unique way. It represents the festive and communal soul of Mexico City while preserving living customs that date back to pre-Hispanic times.
